1.explanation:
1. src/js/components/DataTable/README.md – shows the DataTable API and configuration options, including sort properties.  
2. src/js/components/DataTable/stories/typescript/Basic.tsx – a minimal example illustrating how DataTable sorting is invoked in TypeScript, useful to reproduce the null/undefined behavior.  
3. src/js/components/DataTable/stories/CustomThemed/Basic.js – themed example demonstrating the sort UI; helps verify that styling or theming isn’t interfering with sort logic.  
4. src/js/components/TableHeader/README.md – defines how sortable headers are implemented, including the click handler and display of sort icons.  
5. src/js/components/Table/README.md – underlying Table component documentation used by DataTable for rendering rows and headers.  
6. src/js/utils/sort.js – the utility responsible for comparing values during sort; key to adjusting logic to treat null/undefined as an empty string and fixing the bug.
1.bug_scenario: The screenshot shows a Grommet DataTable with columns “ID”, “Name”, “Parent”, “Order”, and “Children”. When the user clicks the sort control in the “Parent” column header, rows that have a null or undefined Parent value are not being treated as empty strings. Instead of being sorted consistently (e.g., appearing at the top or bottom), they remain out of order relative to other rows with actual string values. The UI elements involved include the DataTable component, its sortable TableHeader cell for “Parent”, and the underlying sort utility that compares cell values (including null or undefined).
